title: Shape Effects: shadow, glow and soft edges for shapes
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #275

## What changed
- **Model** (`crates/doc/src/effects.rs`): `ShapeEffects { shadow, glow, soft_edge }` on `InlineObject::Shape` (shapes and text boxes; serde-defaulted, so existing documents load unchanged). Shadow: colour, transparency, blur, distance, angle. Glow: colour, size, transparency. Soft edges: radius. Every value is sanitised: non-finite values are dropped, transparency is clamped to 0–100 %, blur ≤ 100 pt, distance ≤ 200 pt, glow ≤ 150 pt, soft edge ≤ 100 pt, and the angle is normalised. There are nine outer-shadow presets (Offset: Bottom Right … Top Left, Offset: Center) and no perspective shadows.
- **Command** `shape.effects {"shadow"?: preset|{preset?, color, transparency, blur, distance, angle}|null, "glow"?: pt|{color, size, transparency}|null, "softEdge"?: pt|null}`. An omitted key is left as it is. It applies to every shape in the selection, is one undo step, and updates the object's effect extent so inline shapes leave room for their shadow or glow.
- **Rendering** (vello_cpu screen + krilla PDF): neither backend has a shared blur filter, so both use the same approximation (`effects::bands`). The shape's silhouette is grown or shrunk in steps and overlaid with partial opacity. This gives a linear falloff, so screen and PDF match. The shadow is an offset band centred on the edge (±blur/2), the glow spreads outward over its size, and soft edges fade the fill inward over the radius; with soft edges the outline isn't drawn, because it would sit at the fully faded edge.
- **DOCX**: reads and writes `a:effectLst` in `wps:spPr` with `a:glow` (rad + colour/alpha), `a:outerShdw` (blurRad, dist, dir, algn, rotWithShape, colour/alpha) and `a:softEdge` (rad), in schema order (ECMA-376 §20.1.8). `wp:effectExtent` is at least the effects' reach. On reading, `srgbClr`, `sysClr lastClr` and basic `prstClr` are resolved; theme colours fall back to black for shadows and the default colour for glows. Other effects (inner shadow, reflection, …) were not…

title: Open and save password-protected Word documents (#55)
author: vangel76
body:
## What changes for users

- **Opening a password-protected `.docx`/`.docm`/`.dotx`/`.dotm`** no longer opens a blank document. WordCraft asks for the password, desktop and web alike. A wrong password shows an error and you can try again. Scripts (control channel, MCP, CLI `run`) get an error instead of a dialog. They pass `file.open {"path", "password"}`.
- **File › Info › Protect Document** has two new buttons. **Encrypt with Password…** asks for the password twice. **Remove Password** takes it off. A document opened with a password is saved with it again, as Word does.
- Commands:
  - `file.encrypt {"password": string | null}` replaces the old "isn't available yet" stub. `null` or `""` removes the password. The command is pure, so the password never ends up in Repeat or in a recorded macro.
  - `file.save` / `file.saveAs` take `"password"?`.
  - `file.open` takes `"password"?`.
  - `file.info` and `file.open`/`file.save` results report `"encrypted"`.

## What's supported

- **Agile encryption** ([MS-OFFCRYPTO] §2.3.4.10–2.3.4.15), the default since Office 2010:
  - **Reading:** AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256 in CBC mode, with SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512.
  - **Steps on open:** derive the password key using `spinCount`, check the password verifier, check the data-integrity HMAC, then decrypt the package in 4096-byte segments.
  - **Writing:** AES-256 + SHA-512 with spinCount 100000 (Word's defaults). The output includes the `\x06DataSpaces` streams from §2.1 / §2.3.4.1–3.
- **Not supported, with a clear error:** Standard encryption (Office 2007, version x.2), extensible encryption, certificate-only key encryptors, and legacy `.doc` RC4. Standard encryption would be a small follow-up.
- The format comes from Microsoft's public Open Specification [MS-OFFCRYPTO] and [MS-CFB], via the existing `cfb` crate. No code was copied from anywhere.

All pure Rust and wasm-compatible. They are added to the workspace and used by `wordcra…

title: Linux: the title bar carries the window controls, as in Word
author: gyurix
body:
## What

On X11 the window manager draws its own title bar above the one the app already
has, so every window has two bars. Only the outer one carries minimize,
maximize and close, and it does not match the app it belongs to.

This turns the system frame off on Linux and FreeBSD and draws the controls in
the app's own title bar, which is where Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Acrobat put
them. The window still resizes, moves, maximizes and closes exactly as before.

## Why not leave the window manager's frame in place

It is not a matter of taste, in two places:

- **DeckCraft** draws the presentation full screen, and **PdfCraft** has a
  full-screen page view; in both, a system title bar would sit over the content.
- With client-side decorations the controls follow the app's own theme, so they
  stay legible in the dark theme instead of being a light bar on a dark window.

## How it was checked

Each app was built from this branch, installed as a `.deb` and driven with
`xdotool` on XFCE/xfwm4, 1920x1080:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| maximize / restore buttons | `_NET_WM_STATE` gains and loses `MAXIMIZED_HORZ`/`MAXIMIZED_VERT` |
| double-click on the title bar | same, in both directions |
| move by dragging the title bar | window moves |
| resize from all four edges | window resizes |
| resize from all four corners | window resizes diagonally |
| minimize, then reactivate | `_NET_WM_STATE_HIDDEN` set, then cleared |
| close | window closes, through the same unsaved-changes check |
| slideshow / full screen (DeckCraft, PdfCraft) | no controls drawn over the content |
| overlay screens (Backstage, palette) | controls stay reachable, drawn last |

## Compatibility

- macOS and Windows are untouched; both keep the system frame.
- `<APP>_SYSTEM_TITLEBAR=1` keeps the window manager's title bar, for anyone who
  prefers it or whose window manager needs a frame to place the window.
- The three new tooltip strings (`Minimize`, `Maximize`, `Restore Down`) are
  added to every f…

title: Gridlines: the document's own grid spacing, and table gridlines on by default (follow-up to #243)
author: dkhlapov
body:
Follow-up to #243, as asked in #231. Refs #69.

Ports the two things #231 did that #243 doesn't:

## The document's own grid spacing
DOCX stores the drawing grid in `settings.xml` as `w:drawingGridHorizontalSpacing` and `w:drawingGridVerticalSpacing` (ECMA-376 §17.15.1.44/45).
- `wordcraft-doc`: new `Settings.grid_h` / `grid_v` and `DEFAULT_GRID`.
- `wordcraft-docx`: reads both (clamped to 0.5–1584 pt) and writes them back only when they differ from the default.
- `canvas.rs`: View › Gridlines draws at the document's spacing, across and down separately. #243's thinning when zoomed far out is kept.

**One behaviour change to look at:** a document that doesn't state a spacing now gets the spec's default of 180 twentieths of a point (1/8 inch, 9 pt) instead of #243's fixed 0.5 cm (about 14 pt), so the default grid is a bit denser. If you'd rather keep 0.5 cm as the on-screen default, it's a one-line change to `DEFAULT_GRID`; the reading and writing don't depend on it.

## Table gridlines on by default
`table.viewGridlines` (Table Layout › View Gridlines) starts on, as in Word, so tables without borders still show their cells. `ViewState.table_gridlines` deserializes to `true` when missing.

## Verification
- `settings_core_theme_round_trip` now sets a non-default grid (5.5 pt across, 18 pt down) and checks it survives a save and reopen.
- #243's `drawing_grid` tests now also cover separate across/down spacing and fall back to the spec default for zero, negative, NaN and infinite spacings.
- `page_and_table_gridlines_toggle_independently` checks the new table default.
- `cargo xtask ci` on Linux, on `main` as of #234 (after rebasing onto current `main`, the doc, docx, engine and ui-egui tests pass again): fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass. All tests pass except the four font-dependent ones that also fail on unmodified `main` on this machine (`tests_bidi::persian_letters_join_and_brackets_mirror`, `tests_bidi::glyph_runs_carry_their_text_for_pdf_export`, `tests::…

title: Tests: the floating header text box test passes on FreeBSD (no font-dependent numbers)
author: vangel76
body:
## Failing CI
The "FreeBSD 14 (build + test)" job fails on `main`, e.g. https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/actions/runs/38070909002 (job 114267944961):

```
tests::floating_header_text_box_leaves_the_body_at_the_top_margin panicked at crates/layout/src/tests.rs:2057:5:
control body starts at the top margin: 72.597595
```

## Cause
The test (from #242) puts a two-line header 36pt from the top of the page and expects the body of the *control* document (no text box) to start at the 72pt top margin. The height of those two lines depends on which font the default text resolves to. With the usual Linux/macOS fonts they fit under 72pt. With only WordCraft's bundled fonts (the FreeBSD VM has no matching system fonts), they end at 72.6pt, so the header correctly pushes the body down. The failing check is the control's own sanity check. The floating text box never changed the layout. This is not a product bug.

Reproduced locally by hiding the system fonts (`bwrap --dev-bind / / --tmpfs /usr/share/fonts --setenv HOME /nonexistent <test binary> floating_header`). It fails with the same `72.597595`.

## Fix
The header now starts 18pt from the top, so the two header lines fit well above the top margin with any font. Every check is the same as before:
- the control body starts at the top margin
- the floating box changes neither where the body starts nor the page count
- the same box placed inline still pushes the body down

## Verified
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout floating_header` passes with the system fonts and with them hidden (bundled fonts only)
- `cargo test -p wordcraft-layout`: all tests pass except the two known environment failures fixed by #261 (`fragmented_hidden_text_lays_out_like_the_visible_text`, `tests_bidi::glyph_runs_carry_their_text_for_pdf_export`)
- `cargo clippy -p wordcraft-layout --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean

title: Desktop: File › Print opens the document in the system PDF viewer for printing
author: vangel76
body:
## What changed

The desktop app now has a print route. Until now, File › Print on desktop only offered export. It now shows the **Print** button, the same one the web version got in #209. Clicking it renders the document to PDF through the existing export path, writes the PDF to a new temporary file (`wordcraft-print-<pid>-<time>-<n>.pdf` in the OS temp folder), and opens that file in the system's PDF viewer without blocking the window. You then print from the viewer through the system print dialog.

How the file is opened on each OS:
- **Linux / BSD:** the default PDF app, using the `open` crate (`xdg-open`, then `gio`, `gnome-open`, `kde-open`, `wslview`).
- **macOS:** Preview (`open -a Preview <pdf>`). If that fails, the default app opens it instead. The wait runs on a background thread.
- **Windows:** the default app for `.pdf`, using the `open` crate (PowerShell `Start-Process`, with an Explorer fallback). No `cmd /C start` quoting and no `unsafe`.

Details:
- `open` 5.4 was already in `Cargo.lock` through `egui_kittest`, so the only lock change is one new dependency edge. It is added for non-wasm targets in `apps/wordcraft` only, so OS integration stays in the app crate and nothing changes for wasm or the lower layers.
- The temporary file is created with `create_new` (O_EXCL), so it never overwrites an existing file or follows a planted link. On Unix it is mode 0600.
- If no viewer can be started, the error shows in the status bar ("Print failed: …") and the temporary file is removed.
- The viewer reads the file after the call returns, so the file can't be deleted right away. Print files older than an hour are removed on a background thread when the app starts and after each print. Only regular files matching `wordcraft-print-*.pdf` are touched.
- There is no Quick Print in the ribbon, so I didn't add an `lp` route that skips the dialog.

title: Table sizing: Height/Width boxes, AutoFit to contents and a Table Properties dialog
author: vangel76
body:
## What changed

**Table Layout › Cell Size: Height and Width boxes.** They show the caret cell's row height and column width as laid out on the page, in inches like the ribbon's other length boxes. A row with no set height shows the height its text gives it. Editing a box runs `table.rowHeight` / `table.columnWidth`, so the ribbon, command search, CLI and MCP do the same thing, and dragging a value counts as one Undo. An Exactly row height stays Exactly. `table.columnWidth` now clears the table's preferred width so the layout doesn't scale the column back, and it keeps the cells' saved widths (`w:tcW`) in step with the grid.

**AutoFit Contents now fits the columns to their text.** A new layout helper, `wordcraft_layout::measure_table_columns`, measures what each grid column needs:
- the narrowest width, which fits the longest word (text with no break opportunity);
- the widest width, which fits each paragraph on one line.

Both include indents and cell margins and use the table style's cell formatting. Cells that span several columns spread what they need across those columns.

`autofit_widths` then shares out the text width the way Word does. If every column fits at its widest, each gets its widest. Otherwise each column gets its narrowest plus a share of the remaining room, in proportion to how much wider it would like to be. The result is written into the table grid and cell widths, so it is saved and stays the same when you reopen the document. Measuring stops after 4000 paragraphs, so a huge table only has its first rows measured.

- **Table:** preferred width, alignment (left, center, right), indent from left
- **Row:** height with At least or Exactly, allow the row to break across pages, repeat as header row

title: Tables: autofit by content, and floating tables inside cells
author: naxvog
body:
Picks up what #137 left open: floating tables nested in table cells. Along the way, tables whose columns may follow their content (`tblLayout` not fixed) now get Word's autofit.

**Autofit**
- We always used the stored grid. Word sizes autofit columns from what's in them.
- A table with no preferred width anywhere (no `tblW`, no `tcW`, which is what generators write) now takes its columns from their content. Each column gets its widest line if they all fit, else the room is shared between longest word and widest line. In case51 a nested table no longer fills its whole cell, and the document is two pages like Word's instead of one.
- In other autofit tables no column is narrower than its longest word, and the columns with room give up the difference. In case91 "ON" no longer breaks into "O / N".
- Measuring counts list indents, table-style formatting (header row, total row, first column, bands), spanning cells and nested tables. A long unbreakable string can't push the table past its room, and a table of empty cells keeps its grid.
- `tcW w:type="pct"` is now read and written back (`CellProps::width_pct`), so such a table isn't treated as having no preferred width.

**Floating tables in cells**
- They now stand at their position in the cell and take no room. The text after them wraps around them, a table that may not overlap moves below the ones in its way, and the cell grows to hold them.
- In headers and footers they don't move the header or footer text.
- A row whose lines all fit, but whose nested floating table runs past the page bottom, now splits there instead of jumping to the next page whole.

**Wrapping gap:** text now flows beside a floating object into gaps of 20pt or more (was 36pt). Word puts a paragraph beside a floating table in a 21.3pt gap but not in an 18.6pt one; docxide-pdf's case139–148 vary only that distance. On the full corpus no other document changed.

**Not done:** when a nested floating table doesn't fit on the page, Word moves the whole …

title: Charts and SmartArt: draw them instead of dropping them
author: naxvog
body:
Charts and SmartArt diagrams were dropped on import. They took no room, so the text after them moved up: five of the six chart documents in docxide-pdf's corpus came out a page short. Nothing was drawn either.

**What changed**
- A chart or diagram is now an `InlineObject::Graphic`. It takes its room, floats and wraps like a picture, and draws a list of neutral items: shapes, paths, one-line texts and pictures. Layout scales the items to the object's box, and render and pdf draw them (new `Draw::Path`).
- **Charts** (`docx/read/chart.rs`) are drawn from the values the chart part caches:
  - clustered, stacked and 100% bar and column charts;
  - line, area, pie, doughnut and scatter charts;
  - title, legend, gridlines and axis labels;
  - Excel number and date formats.
- **SmartArt** (`docx/read/diagram.rs`) is drawn from the drawing Word stores beside the diagram: preset shapes, theme colours, text and pictures.
- Theme-colour handling is shared by both (`docx/read/drawing_color.rs`).
- Each chart or diagram part is read once, only through a relationship of its type, under a per-file budget of items, so a crafted file can't blow up memory.
- Tagged PDF tags them as figures with their alt text. The accessibility check reports charts without alt text, and HTML and Markdown export the alt text as an image's.

**Not done**
- Charts and diagrams aren't written back when saving a .docx. They weren't before either, so nothing is lost that wasn't lost already. To avoid edits that would vanish on save, the editor lets you select and delete them but not move or resize them.
- Radar, stock, 3-D and combination charts draw their first supported chart type only.
- SmartArt pictures aren't clipped to their shape.

title: Pictures: draw WMF and EMF pictures instead of a grey box
author: naxvog
body:
Windows metafiles (WMF, EMF) couldn't be decoded and showed as grey boxes, on screen and in PDF. Older documents use them a lot for logos, crests and diagrams; 12 of the 365 documents in docxide-pdf's corpus have them.

**What changed**
- New crate `wordcraft-metafile` (layer 1, depends only on kurbo and thiserror). It reads both formats from the public [MS-WMF] and [MS-EMF] specifications into paths and bitmaps, and fits them into a picture's box. `render` and `pdf` paint the result as vectors.
- **Supported:**
  - lines, polygons, curves, rectangles, ellipses and arcs, and path brackets;
  - pens and brushes, including the stock ones;
  - the mapping modes and world transforms;
  - bitmaps in DIB form, with the raster operations Office pictures use (copy, mask, paint, alpha blend).
- **Input is treated as hostile.** Every read is bounds-checked and every size is checked arithmetic, also on wasm32. A byte budget caps what one picture may allocate. A fuzz test feeds truncated, random and mutated files.
- The parsed pictures are cached, bounded by bytes, and keyed so that freed media can't alias.

**Not done:** text records (`ExtTextOut`) and EMF+ records are skipped, so a metafile that is mostly text shows only its lines and fills.

**Effect** (Measured with docxide-pdf's scorer, `page-metrics` at 150 dpi, against the 365 Word-exported reference PDFs in its test corpus. Both runs use the same open substitute fonts, so the absolute scores are low; compare the before and after numbers, not the levels. "Before" is main plus #135, which is still open.)

The pictures in all five corpus documents I checked by eye now match Word's: the coats of arms in two Australian acts, a logo in an auditor's report, a crest in a footer, and a logo strip. They are a small part of their pages, so the scores move little: one more document with ink overlap ≥ 20.5% (208 → 209), five documents up to 3 SSIM points better, none worse.

**Tests:** about 50 metafile tests, one per record family …

title: Phonetic Guide: ruby text (furigana, pinyin) over base text
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #288

## What changed
Home › Font › **Phonetic Guide** (`format.phonetic`) puts small ruby text (furigana, pinyin…) over the selected text.

- **Model**: `InlineObject::Ruby` anchored at U+FFFC like other inline objects: base text, ruby text, alignment (ECMA-376 `ST_RubyAlign`: center, distributeLetter, distributeSpace, left, right, rightVertical), ruby size, raise (baseline to baseline), base size, language, and the ruby's own run formatting. Its plain text is the base, so find, word count and TXT/HTML/MD exports read the base text, and selection and the caret treat the ruby as one unit (like fields).
- **Layout**: the base is drawn in its run's formatting and the ruby above it at its size, placed by alignment. When the ruby is wider than the base, the ruby sets the width and the base is centred under it. The line grows to fit the ruby. It is drawn in the shared display list, so screen and PDF both show it.
- **DOCX**: `w:ruby` is read and written with `w:rubyPr` (`w:rubyAlign`, `w:hps`, `w:hpsRaise`, `w:hpsBaseText`, `w:lid`), `w:rt` and `w:rubyBase` runs, keeping their text and run formatting. Before this, only the base text was kept and the ruby was dropped.
- **Command**: `format.phonetic {"ruby": string|null, "align"?, "size"?, "offset"?}` works on the selection, or on the ruby the selection is or the caret is next to. It sets one ruby group over the whole selection, edits an existing ruby, or removes it with `null` or `""`, and it can be undone. Called without `ruby`, it asks the UI for the dialog and returns the selection's phonetic guide (`base`, `ruby`, `align`, `size`, `offset`). The default ruby size is half the base size, rounded down to a half point.
- **UI**: a Phonetic Guide button (drawn in code) in Home › Font, and a dialog with the base text, ruby text, alignment, offset, size and Remove. title: Linux: the display theme asks the desktop, not winit
author: gyurix
body:
## What

`Display theme ▸ Use system setting` does not follow the system on Linux.

winit reports no system theme there: `ActiveEventLoop::system_theme()` is `None`
on every Linux desktop, in every version of winit, so
`Appearance::is_dark(ctx.system_theme())` always saw `None` and drew light. The
setting is honest on macOS and Windows, where winit answers; here it was a
promise with nothing behind it.

## The fix

`desktop_theme` asks the XDG Desktop Portal's `Settings` interface for
`org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme`, on a thread of its own so no D-Bus
call is ever made from the frame loop. That schema name is asked first because
GNOME's portal and XFCE's both answer it; the older
`org.freedesktop.interface.color-scheme` is asked second, which is the one KDE's
portal answers. The first answer is delivered straight away and the frame loop
drains it each frame, so switching the desktop theme while WordCraft is running
is picked up within a few seconds.

A desktop that answers neither schema leaves the user's own choice standing, and
`Light` and `Dark` are untouched: only what `System` resolves to changes. macOS
and Windows keep asking winit, and the portal thread simply never answers.

Nothing else moves — `theme::Appearance`, the saved `theme` key, the
`legacy_dark` migration and the `ui.theme` command are all as they were, because
they are already right.

## How it was checked

Built from this branch and run on XFCE with
`gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme`:

| step | saved preference | drawn |
|---|---|---|
| fresh start, desktop dark | `system` | **dark** (was light) |
| desktop set to `prefer-light` | `system` | **light**, within a few seconds |
| desktop set back to `prefer-dark` | `system` | **dark**, within a few seconds |
| `Light` or `Dark` chosen, then the desktop changes | that choice | unchanged |

title: Enclose Characters: put a character in a circle, square, triangle or diamond
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #297

## What changed
- **Command** `format.enclose {"shape": "circle|square|triangle|diamond" | null, "style"?: "shrink|enlarge", "text"?: string}` works on one full-width character or up to two half-width ones (anything else is an error). The `text` parameter is the dialog's Text box: it replaces the selection, or goes in at the caret.
- **Model:** enclosed characters are an `EQ` field with the overstrike switch, as ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.5.20 describes: `eq \o\ac(○,字)`. An enclosure symbol is drawn as a vector `Draw::Shape` (ellipse, rectangle, triangle or diamond) in the text colour, so it doesn't depend on the font having ○□△◇:
  - "Shrink text": the text is scaled to fit inside a shape one em high.

title: AutoSave switch is greyed out, with the reason, when AutoSave can't save
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause

AutoSave writes only a file the user saved in this session, in a format that keeps everything (`.docx`, `.docm`, `.dotx`, `.dotm`, `.odt`, `.rtf`, `.json`). But the title-bar switch only checked "saved here", so:

- **#196 (desktop):** after saving a `.md` (or `.txt`, `.html`…) file the switch showed **on**, while `autosave_tick` silently skipped the file because the format can't keep all formatting.
- **#176 (web):** in the browser, saving is a download; there is no file AutoSave could keep writing to. The switch and the File › Options checkbox still looked usable, and nothing explained that edits weren't saved.

Separately, the `file.autosave` command (scripts, MCP) toggled an engine flag that the app never read.

## Change

- `WordApp::autosave_block()` says why AutoSave can't cover the document, or `None` when it can: **browser**, **never saved**, **format that can't keep everything** (by file name), or **opened but not saved here**. `autosaves()` = AutoSave on and not blocked, so the switch never shows on while nothing is saved.

Save as .docx to turn on AutoSave."* On the desktop, clicking it opens Save As (suggesting `.docx`), and AutoSave turns on once that save goes through. title: Open Word documents with WordCraft by default (file associations + Options button)
author: vangel76
body:
Makes it easy to open `.docx` and friends with WordCraft from the file manager, and to make WordCraft the default app where the system allows it. Installers register WordCraft for these types but never take over an existing default.

## Windows (MSI, `packaging/windows/wordcraft.wxs`)
- A new `WordcraftFileTypes` component, with its own new GUID (not used by any sibling app; the packaging-lint checks pass).
- One ProgId per type: `.docx .docm .dotx .dotm .doc .dot .rtf .odt`. Each has the app icon and the open command `"[#WordcraftExe]" "%1"`, which is the same path as `[INSTALLFOLDER]wordcraft.exe`.
- Each extension lists its ProgId under `OpenWithProgids`, and `Applications\wordcraft.exe` lists the types under `SupportedTypes` and sets `FriendlyAppName`. This makes WordCraft show up in Explorer's **Open with**.
- `Software\WordCraft\Capabilities` (with `FileAssociations` for the Word/RTF/ODT types) is registered under `RegisteredApplications`, so WordCraft appears in **Settings › Default apps**.
- `.md` and `.txt` get ProgIds and Open With entries only. They are not listed under Capabilities, so they are never offered as default claims.
- Nothing writes an extension's default value, so no existing default is taken over.

## Linux / BSD
- The desktop entry already had `Exec=wordcraft %F`. It now also declares the macro-enabled, template and legacy Word types (`application/vnd.ms-word.*`, `…wordprocessingml.template`, `application/msword`, `application/msword-template`) and `text/rtf`.
- The AppStream metainfo lists the document types as `<mediatype>`.
- deb, rpm, AppImage and both Flatpak manifests install this same desktop file (checked in `package.sh` and the manifests).

title: Draw tables and split or merge cells with a pen and eraser
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #303

## What changed
- **Engine (`crates/engine/src/cmd/table_draw.rs`)**
  - `table.draw {"page", "x0", "y0", "x1", "y1"}` takes a pen stroke in page points.
    - A rectangle at least 12 pt each way, drawn outside any table, inserts a one-cell table at the paragraph under the stroke's start. The table goes before the paragraph if the stroke starts at the paragraph's beginning (or the paragraph is empty), otherwise after it. The rectangle's width becomes the table's preferred width and its left offset becomes the indent. Its height becomes the row's at-least height.
    - A straight **vertical** line inside a table splits each cell it crosses into two columns at that x. If the x lands within 3 pt of an existing grid line, it uses that line. Otherwise it adds a new grid column, and the other rows' cells span it via gridSpan.
    - A straight **horizontal** line splits the row it crosses at that y. The crossed cells become two. The row's other cells span both rows as a vertical merge (vMerge restart/continue), and the row height is divided at the line.
  - `table.eraser {"page", "x", "y"}` removes the border between two cells within 4 pt of the point by merging the cells.
    - A vertical border is merged horizontally with `Table::merge_right` (gridSpan).
    - A horizontal border becomes a vertical merge (vMerge). The lower cell's text moves into the merged cell, and the merge joins an existing merged group above it.
  - Each call is one undo step. Bad params, empty spots, and hostile or non-finite coordinates return errors and never panic.
  - Some cases are refused on purpose, each with a clear error:
    - A line that crosses only part of a vertically merged cell.
    - A horizontal split through a vertically merged cell.
    - Erasing a vertical border next to a vertically merged cell.
    - A border between cells above and below that don't line up.
    - Drawing a rectangle inside a table (nested tables).

title: Linux: match the desktop scale instead of the panel's DPI
author: gyurix
body:
XRandR reports the panel's physical DPI while the desktop renders at 96, so winit scales every window up and the app looks zoomed for no reason. Pin WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR to 1 in the desktop launcher so menu and panel launches match the desktop.

Same fix as the local WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR=1 default; baked into the shipped launcher so installs work without system patches. Terminal launches can still export their own value.

title: System interface theme follows OS changes again, and Dark page no longer darkens the interface
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause

Both bugs come from my System theme change (#249). Thanks to @coygeek for the detailed audits in #311 and #312.

- **#311:** with Interface theme = System, `theme::apply` resolved the OS appearance and called `ctx.set_theme(Light/Dark)`. egui's `sync_window_theme` (on by default) turns that into `ViewportCommand::SetTheme(Light/Dark)`, egui-winit calls `window.set_theme(Some(..))`, and on macOS winit sets an explicit `NSAppearance`. winit's `effectiveAppearance` observer returns early while an appearance is set, so `ThemeChanged` never arrives again and egui's cached system theme goes stale: System stopped following the OS after the first frame.
- **#312:** the frame logic used `theme.is_dark(os) || view.dark_mode`, so turning on Dark page made the whole interface dark even with System (OS light) or Light selected.

## Change

- `theme::apply` now takes the `Appearance` setting and installs **both** palettes: our light visuals as egui's light style and our dark visuals as its dark style (`set_visuals_of`), with the shared spacing and text styles applied to both (`all_styles_mut`). So when the OS changes, egui switches to our other palette, not its default style. That style swap is the problem #249 tried to avoid by pinning.
- System sets `ThemePreference::System` with `fallback_theme = Light` (the documented fallback when the OS reports nothing), so egui sends `SetTheme(SystemDefault)` and the native window keeps reporting OS changes. Manual Light/Dark still pin the window, as before.
- `apply` runs only when the setting changes. egui handles the OS switch itself, and `Tokens::get` keeps reading the active style.
- Dark page now affects only the pages. The interface follows the Interface theme setting alone, like Word, where the page colour switch is separate from the Office theme.
- Docs: `docs/ui-parity.md` row and revision history, and the `ROADMAP.md` progress log. No user-facing strings changed. The existing Dark page tooltip already describes it as a…

title: Windows: smooth again on older graphics without a DirectX 12 driver
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause

Since #50 the Windows build initializes only DirectX 12 (OpenGL stays off by default because creating it can crash AMD's `atio6axx.dll`). On PCs whose graphics chip has no DirectX 12 driver — Intel 4th-generation graphics on Windows 11 in #316 — DirectX 12 only offers WARP, Microsoft's software renderer, so every frame is drawn on the CPU and the app lags. `WGPU_BACKEND=GL` makes it smooth.

## Change

`apps/wordcraft/src/graphics.rs`, Windows only, when no `WGPU_BACKEND` override is set: before eframe creates its instance, a short-lived DirectX 12-only wgpu instance enumerates the adapters and checks each against the limits eframe's own device descriptor will request. Then `choose_backends(override, adapters)` (a pure function) decides:

- `WGPU_BACKEND` set → exactly that, as before (the probe doesn't run).
- A hardware DirectX 12 adapter that meets eframe's limits → DirectX 12 only (unchanged for everyone with a working driver, so AMD machines never get GL).
- Only WARP (`DeviceType::Cpu`) → OpenGL **plus** DirectX 12. wgpu ranks any GPU above a software adapter, so the OpenGL GPU is used; WARP stays as a last resort for machines with no OpenGL driver either (VMs, remote desktop) so they still open instead of failing to find an adapter.
- No DirectX 12 adapter, or only GPUs below eframe's limits → OpenGL alone (so a DirectX 12 GPU that would fail device creation isn't picked over the OpenGL one).

The adapters and the decision are logged (`graphics:` lines in the log file). README troubleshooting (next to `WGPU_BACKEND`) explains the fallback; hardware-parity, gaps #3 and the progress log are updated.

## Testing

- Unit tests for `choose_backends`: override wins (also over a WARP-only probe); WARP only → GL + DX12; nothing → GL; GPU below limits → GL; any usable GPU → DX12 only.
- `cargo check -p wordcraft --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `cargo clippy -p wordcraft --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings` pass (cross-compiled f…

title: Long display equations wrap across lines like Word
author: vangel76
body:
## Change

A display equation (`m:oMathPara`) wider than its column used to run off the page. Now it wraps the way Word does:

- **Break points:** top-level binary operators and relations only (`=`, `<`, `≤`, `≈`, `+`, `−`, `±`, `×`, `·`, `÷`, …). Nothing breaks inside fractions, radicals, scripts or matrices. A unary minus is not a break point.
- **Greedy fill:** each line takes as many terms as fit. If one term is wider than the line, it overflows rather than breaking inside.
- **`m:brkBin`:** the break goes before the operator (the default), after it, or the operator appears on both lines (repeat). With repeat, `m:brkBinSub` (`--`, `-+`, `+-`) decides how a minus is repeated.
- **Continuation lines:** indented by `m:wrapIndent` (default 1440 twips = 1 inch, capped at half the line), or set flush right when `m:wrapRight` is on. The first line starts at the left, and an automatically wrapped equation fills the column.
- **Manual breaks:** `m:brk` on a run starts a new line. With `m:alnAt="n"`, that line's operator lines up under the n-th operator of the first line.
- Inline equations, numbered equations (`#`) and `m:jc` alignment are unchanged.

Model / DOCX:
- `Settings.math: Option<MathProps>` reads `m:mathPr` from settings.xml (`brkBin`, `brkBinSub`, `wrapIndent` / `wrapRight`) and writes it back. `MRun.brk` reads `m:brk` / `m:alnAt` in a math run's `m:rPr` and writes it back.
- Documents that have neither save exactly as before.

Progress docs updated: `docs/gaps.md` #29, `docs/layout-parity.md`, `docs/file-format-parity.md`.

## Testing

- `crates/layout/src/math.rs`:
  - `long_display_equations_wrap_before_operators_and_indent`: a long sum breaks into 2 or more lines inside the column. Each continuation line starts with `+` one wrap indent in. Also covers the after and repeat (+ wrapRight) modes, inline equations not wrapping, and an over-wide fraction overflowing instead of breaking.

title: View › Window: Switch Windows, Arrange All, View Side by Side and Synchronous Scrolling
author: vangel76
body:
## Design

WordCraft has one document per process: each window is its own `wordcraft` process, and File › New/Open replace the document in place (`view.newWindow` and `view.split` are still placeholders). So these four commands work **across processes** rather than through a multi-document redesign:

- **Window registry.** At start, every desktop window binds `127.0.0.1` on a free port, picks a random id and a 256-bit key, and writes `<settings>/windows/<id>.json` (`{"id","port","key","title"}`, mode 0600 on Unix, written atomically). It rewrites the file every 30 s and removes it on exit. A background thread lists the folder every second and pings each entry. An entry whose port refuses connections, or that doesn't answer and is more than 2 minutes old (needed on Windows, which doesn't refuse a closed port right away), is left over from a crash and gets removed. Malformed, oversized or mismatched entries are ignored.
- **Peer channel, not the control channel.** The full control channel (`--control`) stays opt-in. The new listener accepts one JSON line per connection, `{"key","from","msg"}`, and only these messages: `ping`, `focus`, `place {x,y,width,height}`, `sideBySide {on}`, `syncScroll {on}` and `scroll {dy}`. It can't run commands or read the document. Lines are capped at 4 KiB, the key is compared in constant time, a connection has 2 s to send its line, at most 16 connections are served at once, and numbers are checked (finite, ±32768 pt, scroll ≤ 10⁶).
- **Commands.** The engine `CommandSpec`s (`view.switchWindows {window?}`, `view.arrangeAll`, `view.sideBySide {value?, window?}`, `view.syncScroll {value?}`) record state in `Session::windows` and push UI requests. They are disabled when no window host exists (web, CLI, headless MCP). `ui.inspect` reports `windows.others` (id and title) for agents.
- **UI.** The window list never blocks the UI thread because the background thread refreshes it and sends the messages.
  - **Switch Windows:** a dropdown of the o…

title: Charts, SmartArt and OLE objects are no longer lost when you save a .docx
author: vangel76
body:
## Cause

Since #292 WordCraft reads and draws charts and SmartArt diagrams, but the DOCX writer skipped them (`InlineObject::Graphic { .. } => {}`). OLE objects (`w:object`: embedded workbooks, documents, packages, ActiveX) were read as their picture alone. So opening a document and saving it dropped them without warning, along with every part behind them (chart part, embedded workbook, SmartArt data and layout, OLE embedding).

## Change

- **Reading** (`crates/docx/src/read/embed.rs`): for every chart, diagram and OLE object, the reader keeps the object's own markup (the `a:graphic`, or the whole `w:object`) as a new `wordcraft_doc::graphic::Embedded` on the model object (`Graphic::source` for charts/SmartArt, `InlineObject::Image::ole` for OLE objects). Every part that markup reaches through relationships is kept recursively as opaque bytes in `Document::passthrough`, the mechanism the VBA project already uses. Each part's content type and relationships go in a manifest (`wordcraft:embedded.parts`). For SmartArt, the drawing relationship named in the data part (`dsp:dataModelExt relId`) is kept too.
- **Writing** (`crates/docx/src/write/embed.rs`): each object is written with fresh relationship ids pointing at the re-added parts. Each part keeps its own relationship ids, so the chart XML's `c:externalData r:id` still resolves, and its content type is written as an override. A chart or diagram gets its frame (`wp:inline`/`wp:anchor`, extent, position, wrap) from the object's current size and position, so moving or resizing it in WordCraft is kept; the graphic inside stays as read. An OLE object gets its new size (and offset, if it floats) written into its VML shape style and any `wp:extent`, and fresh `wp:docPr` ids.
- **Name clashes and copies**: a part whose name WordCraft already writes (media, headers, styles…) is renamed. If an object was copied and pasted, each copy gets its own renamed copies of all its parts, so they stay independent in Word (including th…

title: fix(theme): Dark page overrides System light interface chrome
author: Totopo27
body:
## Cause

In `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, `WordApp::logic` computed whether to apply the dark UI theme Tokens as:

```rust
let dark = self.ui.theme.is_dark(ctx.system_theme()) || self.session.view.dark_mode;
```

Because of the unconditional `|| self.session.view.dark_mode`, enabling "Dark page" (`view.darkMode`, which only controls document paper rendering) forced the entire interface chrome (ribbon, tabs, background, ruler, status bar) into the Dark theme, overriding the user's interface theme preference (e.g. `System` on Light OS or explicit `Light`).

## Change

- Decoupled `self.session.view.dark_mode` from interface chrome theme evaluation in `WordApp::logic`:
  ```rust
  let dark = self.ui.theme.is_dark(ctx.system_theme());
  ```
- Retained the document canvas dark paper handling intact in `canvas.rs` (`app.session.view.dark_mode`).
- Added unit test `dark_page_does_not_override_interface_theme` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` verifying that when `ui.theme` is `system` and OS reports `Light`, enabling `view.darkMode` keeps the interface chrome theme light (`applied_dark == Some(false)`) while preserving `session.view.dark_mode == true`.

Fixes #312

title: Rotate and flip pictures, shapes and text boxes freely
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #332

## What changed
- **Model** (minimal, additive): `Float` gets `rot` (degrees clockwise, normalised to 0–360, NaN → 0), `flipH`, `flipV` (serde-skipped when unset). Geometry lives in a new `wordcraft_geom::Spin` (matrix, apply/unapply, rotated bounds, composing a group member's spin with its group's).
- **DOCX** (ECMA-376 §20.1.7.6): reads and writes `a:xfrm` `rot` (60000ths of a degree), `flipH`, `flipV` in `pic:spPr`, `wps:spPr` and `wpg:grpSpPr` (group members keep their own). The `wp:effectExtent` written covers the rotated bounds (effects room + rotation overhang, signed as needed); reading takes the overhang back out so it isn't counted twice. VML `rotation` / `flip` are read too.
- **Layout / render / PDF**: pictures, shapes, charts and groups are drawn turned about their centre (new `Draw::Rotated`, handled by the raster renderer and the PDF writer; rotated inline pictures are still tagged as figures). Square/top-and-bottom wrap uses the rotated bounding box; inline objects reserve their rotated bounds like Word. Hit testing un-rotates the point, so you grab the turned shape, not its old frame. `Placed::Object` / `ObjectHit` carry the spin.
- **Commands**: `arrange.rotate {"direction": "right|left|flipVertical|flipHorizontal"}` (old `flipH`/`flipV` still accepted) now changes the angle and flips instead of rewriting pixels, for pictures, shapes, text boxes and groups. A flip mirrors what's on the page, so a rotated object's angle reverses too. New `arrange.rotation {"degrees", "flipH"?, "flipV"?}` sets an exact angle. Both are undoable. Catalog: Picture Format › Size › Rotation.
- **UI**: a rotation handle above the top-centre of the selection frame. Dragging it turns an outline live and shows the angle, Shift snaps to 15°, and releasing runs one `arrange.rotation`. title: Mail merge: use Excel and OpenDocument spreadsheets as recipient lists
author: vangel76
body:
## What changed

**Select Recipients › Use an Existing List…** now opens Excel (`.xlsx`, `.xlsm`) and OpenDocument (`.ods`) spreadsheets as well as CSV/TSV.

- **Parser** (`crates/formats/src/sheet.rs`, new, L2): a read-only reader written from ECMA-376 Part 1 §18 (SpreadsheetML) and OASIS ODF 1.3. It reuses the zip and quick-xml crates the workspace already has. It lists a workbook's sheets (`workbook.xml` + rels, or the names of the `table:table` elements in `content.xml`; chart sheets are skipped) and reads one sheet into rows of strings:
  - xlsx: shared strings (rich-text runs joined, phonetic runs skipped), inline strings, numbers, booleans (`TRUE`/`FALSE`), errors, cached formula results (`<v>`), sparse cells (`r="C5"` gaps), out-of-order rows. Merged cells keep only the top-left value.

title: Equation gallery: group multi-letter operands in two templates (Yields, n×n Matrix)
author: dkhlapov
body:
**Equation › Operator › Yields** showed only **y** above the arrow instead of "yields". The **n×n Matrix** template had the same problem: it subscripted only "1" and "m" in a₁ₙ, aₘ₁ and aₘₙ.

**Test:** `math_gallery::tests::multi_letter_operands_are_grouped` fails when any template or built-in equation leaves letters directly after a script or limit, which is how a split operand shows up. It fails on both old templates and passes on every other template and built-in equation.

## Commands and shortcuts

| Command | Windows / Linux | macOS | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `para.moveUp` / `para.moveDown` | Alt+Shift+Up / Down | ⌃⇧↑ / ⌃⇧↓ | Moves the paragraph(s) the selection touches above or below the neighbouring paragraph. Edits in the same paragraph update one place rather than adding new ones. Places are not adjusted for later edits; they are clamped to the document when used. |
| `text.toggleUnicode` | Alt+X | (none: Option+X types a character) | Turns the hex code before the caret (up to 6 digits, optional `U+`) or a selected code into its character. Otherwise it turns the character before the caret into its code (`é` ↔ `00E9`). Formatting is kept and it's one undo step. |

title: Balance newspaper columns before a continuous section break
author: vangel76
body:
## What changes

Multi-column sections now end the way they do in Word. When the next section starts **continuous** (`w:type w:val="continuous"` on the following `w:sectPr`, per ECMA-376), the columns on the section's last page are balanced: they share the shortest height that still holds the text, are filled left to right, and the next section starts right below them on the same page. Before this change the text filled the first column and the next section started below the last column.

The same rule covers the end of the document. As in Word, the last section is balanced only when the document ends with a continuous section break (so the multi-column section is followed by an empty continuous section).

Keep lines together, keep with next, widow/orphan control and table rows that can't split still apply. When one of them gets in the way, the columns come out a little uneven (a slightly taller height is used). Unequal column widths (`w:col`) work.

A continuous section also now starts below the **tallest** column on the page. Before, it started below the column that was filled last, which could overlap the taller columns next to it.

## Not balanced
- The section ends with a next-page, even-page, odd-page or next-column break.
- An explicit column break on that page, which already says where the columns end.
- One-column sections, Web/Draft view, and sections with centred or bottom vertical alignment.
- The document's last section when nothing follows it.

## How it works and what it costs
Pagination is still a single pass. For a section that qualifies, the layout saves a small snapshot of its state before each block. The snapshot leaves out the pages, so taking it costs nothing per page. When the section ends, the blocks that reach its last page are laid out again from the saved state, and a binary search on the column height runs over that one page: at most 12 passes plus a final one. A height fits when nothing moves to a new page and nothing runs past it, such …

title: Import: hostile Markdown and HTML no longer take quadratic time
author: g1obalworlds
body:
Found by fuzzing the file readers (about a million mutated inputs across .docx, .odt, .doc, .rtf, .html, .tex, .txt, .json and .md, plus about 300 hand-made hostile files). There were **no panics, stack overflows or out-of-memory crashes**, but three inputs make opening a file hang for tens of seconds. Importers aren't wrapped by `Session::run`, so the UI thread simply blocks.

| Input | Size | Before |
|---|---|---|
| `*[` repeated 50 000 times (`.md`) | 100 KB | 25-41 s |
| `![a](b` repeated 100 000 times (`.md`) | 600 KB | 31-44 s |
| `&#` repeated 500 000 times (`.html`) | 1 MB | 7.5 s (2 MB: 31 s) |

**Causes and changes**
- **Markdown links and images** (`markdown.rs`): every unmatched `[` or `![` rescanned the rest of the text for its `]`, and a destination that doesn't parse was read to the end. Those scans now share a per-paragraph look-ahead budget (8 bytes per byte of text plus 8 KB); once it is used up, further brackets are plain text. Inline tags (`<...>`) are searched within 4 KB and entity names (`&...;`) within 33 bytes.
- **HTML `unescape`** (`html.rs`): searched the whole remaining text for `;` after every stray `&`. It now looks only at the first 33 bytes, which is all an entity name needs.
- **Flow to document** (`model.rs`): appending each inline through `Paragraph::insert_text` rescans and re-normalises every earlier run, so a paragraph with thousands of runs was quadratic by itself. Inlines are now appended directly and the paragraph is normalised once. (This was the biggest part of the `*[` case: parsing took 2 ms, converting took 4 s.)

Ordinary links, images, tags and entities read exactly as before.

**Tests** (`crates/formats/src/tests.rs`)
- `hostile_importer_input_takes_linear_time` runs five hostile inputs (the three above plus `[a](` and `<a`) against a 5 s budget; it takes about 0.1 s now. I checked that it fails without each of the three fixes on its own (the `model.rs` change alone is not enough for the image case, which took 44 s;…

title: Long footnotes continue onto the next page
author: vangel76
body:
## What changes

Long footnotes now flow onto the next page the way Word handles them, instead of pushing the line with the reference off its page.

- If a page's footnotes don't fit below its text, the note that doesn't fit is split at a line boundary. Its first line always stays on the same page as its reference. If even that line doesn't fit, the reference line moves to the next page, as it did before.
- The rest of the note goes at the top of the next page's footnote area, ahead of that page's own notes.
- A page that starts with a continued note gets a full-width continuation separator instead of the short separator.
- A note can keep going across several pages. Once the body text runs out, the remaining part gets pages of its own. Every page places at least one line, so this always ends, and a hard cap backs that up.
- Notes are only split between lines of their own paragraphs, never through a table, picture or text box inside a note. A short note that fits is still placed whole.
- Endnotes are unchanged.

The docx reader currently drops a document's own `w:continuationSeparator` and `w:continuationNotice` footnotes. So the default full-width line is drawn and no "continued" notice appears. This is recorded in `docs/layout-parity.md` and `docs/gaps.md`.

All of the change is in the footnote code in `crates/layout` (`NoteBox`, `PageBuilder::flush_notes`, and the footnote check in `place_para`). Normal pagination is unchanged when the notes fit.

## Testing

- New layout tests:
  - `long_footnotes_continue_on_the_next_page`: the note splits over pages 1–2 and every line is placed exactly once. Page 1 shows the short separator. Page 2 shows the full-width continuation separator, then the rest of the note, then page 2's own note. Body text stays above the notes on both pages.
  - `short_footnotes_stay_whole`.
  - `footnote_longer_than_pages_ends`: a note several pages long continues on pages of its own, and the layout ends.
- These pass: `cargo test -p wordcraft-l…

title: Tight and Through text wrapping follow the object's outline
author: vangel76
body:
## What changes

Text wrapped **Tight** or **Through** around a picture or shape now follows the object's outline instead of its bounding box (before, both behaved like Square).

- **The outline** is the object's wrap polygon (`wp:wrapPolygon`, coordinates in the 21600-unit space of its frame) when it has one. Otherwise it is worked out from the object:
  - shapes: their geometry (ellipse, rounded rectangle, triangle, diamond, arrow, star, heart), flattened to straight lines;
  - pictures: the convex hull of their opaque pixels (alpha ≥ 50% on a grid of at most 48 cells per side, simplified to at most 64 points, crop respected). Pictures without transparency, and JPEGs, use their rectangle;
  - charts and groups: their rectangle.
- The outline **turns and flips with the object** (#340 rotation/flip) and keeps the **distance from text** (distL/distR to the sides, distT/distB above and below).
- **Line layout:** for each line's band, the outline gives the stretch(es) it covers. Tight: text uses the space left and right of the covered stretch. Through: text can also go into gaps inside the outline that are wide enough (the existing 20pt minimum span). A convex outline has no gaps, so it wraps like Tight.
- **DOCX:** `wp:wrapPolygon` round-trips with its `edited` flag for `wrapTight` and `wrapThrough`. The schema requires a polygon, so a shape without one gets its derived outline written, and other objects get their rectangle. When reading, an unedited polygon that covers the whole frame counts as "no polygon", so the outline is still worked out from the object.
- Square, Top and Bottom, Behind Text and In Front of Text are unchanged.

## How it works

- `wordcraft_doc::wrap`: the `WrapPolygon` model (on `Float::wrap_polygon`), shape outlines, and alpha-grid → convex hull.
- `wordcraft_layout::contour`: a `Contour` is built once per placed object, with the points already turned. Each line asks `occupied(top, bottom)` for the stretches it covers, which is one pass over t…

title: Documents keep their own footnote separators and continuation notice
author: vangel76
body:
## Change

Follow-up to #352. The docx reader dropped the special footnotes and endnotes (`w:type` `separator`, `continuationSeparator`, `continuationNotice`, ECMA-376 §17.11), so a document's own separator lines and its continuation notice were lost on screen, in PDF and on save.

- **Model:** `Document::footnote_separators` / `endnote_separators` (`NoteSeparators`) keep the three special notes as paragraphs. The `w:separator` / `w:continuationSeparator` run elements are kept as run objects (`InlineObject::note_separator`).

The separator objects are drawn as a short line or as a line across the column, and any other text or formatting is shown as given. The continuation notice (for example "(continued)") goes under the part of a split footnote that continues on the next page, and only there. The endnote separator is used above the endnotes. Documents without their own keep the default lines exactly as before. Separator and notice text can't be clicked into.
- **DOCX write:** the special notes are written back with Word's ids -1, 0 and 1 and listed in `w:footnotePr` / `w:endnotePr` in settings. When there is a notice, the notes start at id 2. Documents without them get the same default output as before.

Builds on #357; merge that first.

## Testing

- `crates/layout`: `document_note_separators_and_continuation_notice` checks that a split footnote shows the document's separator (short line) on page 1, the "(continued)" notice right under the note's first part inside the page, and the continuation separator (across the text) on page 2. The existing #357 tests (`long_footnotes_continue_on_the_next_page` …) still pass unchanged, so the default rendering hasn't changed.

title: Bump quick-xml to 0.41: the namespace-declaration DoS was reachable (RUSTSEC-2026-0195)
author: pkibiego
body:
## What

Bumps `quick-xml` from 0.38 to 0.41 and adapts the two APIs that changed.

## Why: the advisory was reachable, and the impact is an OOM kill

`crates/docx/src/xml.rs` parses untrusted document XML through `quick_xml::reader::NsReader`. In 0.38.4 that is **RUSTSEC-2026-0195** (CVSS 7.5): the namespace resolver pushes a binding for every `xmlns` / `xmlns:*` declaration on a start tag into an unbounded `Vec` with no limit on the number of declarations.

None of the reader's existing caps bound that path. `MAX_PART` (256 MiB), `MAX_TOTAL` (512 MiB), `MAX_ENTRIES`, `MAX_DEPTH` and `MAX_ELEMENTS` bound part size, entry count, nesting and element count, not declarations per tag.

Measured on current `main` with `wordcraft-cli convert`, using a crafted `.docx` whose `word/document.xml` is a single start tag carrying 21,845,333 `xmlns:a="u"` declarations:

| | |
|---|---|
| On disk | 508 KB |
| Decompressed part | 262 MB (under `MAX_PART`) |
| Peak RSS | **1.19 GB** |
| Exit status | **0** - it opened and converted with no warning |

At the `MAX_PART` / `MAX_TOTAL` ceiling (about 41M declarations across the parts it parses) that is roughly **2.4 GB of resident memory from about a megabyte of download**. For a word processor this is an OOM kill while someone has unsaved work open. Nothing panics, so the `Session::run` `catch_unwind` guard does not catch it - the allocation simply succeeds.

A half-megabyte document from a client or a download link is enough.

## The fix

0.41.0 caps namespace declarations per start tag at 256 (`DEFAULT_MAX_DECLARATIONS_PER_ELEMENT`, raisable through `NamespaceResolver::set_max_declarations_per_element`) and returns `NamespaceError::TooManyDeclarations` beyond it. The same fixture now fails in about a second with a clear error and no namespace allocation:

```
wordcraft-cli: malformed XML: start tag declares more than 256 namespace bindings;
raise the limit with NamespaceResolver::set_max_declarations_per_element
```

Two API changes …

title: Choose which side of an object text wraps on
author: vangel76
body:
**Builds on #360; merge that first.** (This branch contains #360's commit; the new change is the last commit.)

## Change
Square, Tight and Through objects get a wrap side, as in Word's "Wrap text" option: **both sides** (default), **left only**, **right only**, or **largest only**.

title: Right-to-left tables and sections
author: vangel76
body:
## Change

Tables and sections can now run right to left, as in Word (#362). This builds on the paragraph bidi support from #207.

- **RTL tables (`w:tblPr/w:bidiVisual`)**: the grid runs from the right edge, so the first logical column is the rightmost. A start-aligned table (`jc` left/start or none) sits against the right margin, with its indent measured from the right; an end-aligned table sits against the left margin. Each cell's start margin and start (left) border are drawn on its right side. Merged cells (gridSpan/vMerge), turned-text cells and nested tables all follow the mirrored geometry. Hit-testing, the caret and selection use the drawn cell rectangles, and Tab still moves to the next logical cell.
- **RTL sections (`w:sectPr/w:bidi`)**: newspaper columns run right to left, with column 1 on the right (`SectionProps::column_boxes`). The line between columns stays in the middle of each gap. Page numbering is unchanged.
- **Model and .docx**: new `TableProps::bidi_visual`, read and written in schema order (after `tblpPr`/`tblOverlap`, before `tblW`). `SectionProps::rtl` (`w:bidi`) was already read and written and is now laid out.

author: vangel76
body:

title: Rotated or flipped OLE objects keep their turn when saved to .docx
author: vangel76
body:
Follow-up to #333: this rotation write-back was meant to ride along with #333 but missed the merge.

#333 writes OLE objects back from their kept markup at the object's current size, but the rotation and flips from #332 weren't carried into that markup. A turned or flipped OLE object came back unturned (DrawingML) or with its old turn (VML).

author: vangel76
body:

Tools › Customize Keyboard (`tools.customizeKeyboard`, catalog id now live: 403/434, 92.9%).

title: Shape Format › Text: direction, alignment and linked text boxes (#369)
author: vangel76
body:
## What
Implements the Shape Format › Text group: `shape.textDirection`, `shape.alignText` and `shape.link` (Create Link), plus `shape.breakLink` (Break Link).

- **Model** (`doc`): text box parts carry a `TextBody` (`vert`: horz / vert / vert270 / stacked, `anchor`: top / middle / bottom, `next`: the linked box). `Document::text_box_chains()` resolves links. It ignores cycles, self-links and a second box linking to the same target, and caps chains at 256 boxes. Pruning a deleted box clears links to it, and a pasted box keeps its direction and alignment but not its link.
- **Layout** (new `layout/src/textbox.rs`): a text box lays out in its own frame, is cut to what fits, aligned, then turned onto the page with the same turn machinery as table cells' text direction. Stacked text puts one letter on each line. Linked boxes split the first box's story line by line, each box at its own line length (sizes come from the shapes, so the result doesn't depend on layout order). Text past the last box is hidden, as in Word. A linked box reports the first box's story, so clicking into it edits the shared text.
- **DOCX**: reads and writes `wps:bodyPr@vert` / `@anchor` (`ST_TextVerticalType`, `ST_TextAnchoringType`), and `wps:txbx@id` + `wps:linkedTxbx@id/@seq`. Links are resolved after the whole document is read. A repeated seq, a missing first box or a bad seq links nothing.
- **UI**: a Shape Format › Text group with a Text Direction menu (Horizontal, Rotate all text 90°, 270°, Stacked), an Align Text menu (Top, Middle, Bottom) and Create Link. Create Link waits for a click on an empty text box (Esc cancels). Once a box is linked, the button becomes Break Link. Icons are drawn in code. New strings are added to every i18n catalog.

author: vangel76
body:

Tools › Templates and Add-ins (`tools.templates`), the last Templates row in the catalog (402 → 403 of 434).

**Model + DOCX** (ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.15.1)
- `Settings` keeps the attached template (`w:attachedTemplate r:id` → the settings part's `.../attachedTemplate` relationship, written `TargetMode="External"`) and `w:linkStyles`. Both round-trip; they are written in CT_Settings order (after `w:mirrorMargins`, before `w:trackRevisions`). Template paths over 32 KB are dropped on read.

**Engine commands** (programmatic calls never open dialogs)
- `tools.templates` → `{template, linkStyles}` (the ribbon button opens the dialog via `input_dialog`)

title: Citations: eight more bibliography styles (#383)
author: vangel76
body:
## What

WordCraft now formats citations and bibliographies in all 12 of Word's built-in styles. Before this it had 4.

- **New:** Harvard (Anglia), ISO 690 (author-date), ISO 690 (numerical), Turabian, GB/T 7714, GOST (name sort), GOST (title sort), SIST02. **Already there:** APA, MLA, Chicago, IEEE.
- **Table-driven:** each style in `crates/engine/src/cmd/citations.rs` is a `CiteStyle` record. A record sets the in-text form (author-date, author-page or numbered with its brackets), the author name format and separators, the et al. limits, the sort order, and two entry templates (book, journal article). Templates use `{field}` placeholders. A `⟦…⟧` segment is dropped when a field in it is empty, and a full stop never doubles (no "M.." or "Title..”"). Adding a style now means adding data, not more match arms.
- **Numbering:** numbered styles count in order of first citation. GOST counts in its alphabetical name or title order. Inserting a citation renumbers the ones already in the text.
- **IEEE change:** IEEE now numbers by first citation too, as its guide says. Before, it numbered by position in the source list. The output only differs when sources were cited in a different order from the order they were added.

title: Layout: a drop cap in a font over 1000 pt no longer panics
author: g1obalworlds
body:
Found independently by two fuzzers (a stateful command fuzzer and a layout/PDF fuzzer), about 30 million command runs and 25 000 generated documents in total.

**The bug.** `crates/layout/src/para.rs` sized the drop-cap letter with `.clamp(rc.size, 1000.0)`. `f32::clamp` panics when the minimum is greater than the maximum, which happens as soon as the paragraph's text is larger than 1000 pt (Word allows up to 1638). Layout, PDF export and save run outside `Session::run`'s panic guard, so:
- the desktop app panics on every frame once a drop-cap paragraph has a font above 1000 pt;
- `wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.pdf` fails with `min > max, or either was NaN. min = 1638.0, max = 1000.0`.

Reachable from the UI (Font size box up to 1638 plus Drop Cap), a plain .docx with a drop cap and a large font, `styles.modify` on Normal, the CLI, MCP and the control channel. For example:

    wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"Hello world"}' --cmd 'insert.dropCap={"lines":3}' --cmd 'select.all={}' --cmd 'format.size={"size":1001}' --save out.pdf

**The fix.** `.min(1000.0).max(rc.size)`: never panics, and the letter stays at least as large as the text. This was the only `clamp` with data-derived bounds in layout, render, pdf, geom and fonts (checked with grep).

**Test.** `drop_cap_with_a_huge_font_lays_out` lays out a drop-cap paragraph at 999, 1000, 1001 and 1638 pt. Without the fix it fails with exactly the panic above (min = 1001.0, max = 1000.0).

**Checked:** `cargo fmt`, `cargo test --workspace` (no failures), `cargo xtask assets`, `layers`, `wasm` and `parity` pass. I only had a 1.95 toolchain, not the pinned 1.90, so clippy on the whole workspace stops at two lints that 1.95 added in code this PR doesn't touch (`collapsible_match`, `nonminimal_bool`); with those allowed it is clean. Please let CI confirm `cargo xtask ci` on 1.90. No open PR touches this line.

title: Footnote and Endnote options per section (#385)
author: vangel76
body:
Builds on #361 — merge that first (this branch contains its commit; the diff here is the second commit).

title: Content controls: keep, show and edit w:sdt (#381)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #381

## What
Content controls (`w:sdt`, ECMA-376 §17.5.2) are no longer unwrapped on open; they are part of the model and round-trip.

- **Model** (`crates/doc/src/control.rs`): `ContentControl` (id, tag, title/alias, lock, placeholder docPart, showing placeholder, temporary, kind, `w:rPr` / unknown `w:sdtPr` children / `w:sdtEndPr` kept verbatim). Kinds: rich text, plain text (multi-line), `w14:checkbox`, combo box, drop-down list (items + lastValue), date (fullDate, format, lid, calendar, storeMappedDataAs), picture, building block gallery (`docPartObj`/`docPartList`), `w15:repeatingSection` / item. Controls around text are `ControlStart`/`ControlEnd` markers (like range fields), inline or around whole paragraphs; controls whose content starts/ends with a table, and row/cell-level controls (repeating sections), sit on the table/row/cell (`ControlWrap`).
- **DOCX**: reader handles block, inline, row and cell level and nesting (depth-bounded, sizes capped). Writer plans per block list which controls are written inline vs. around blocks so the XML always nests, even after edits (paragraph merges, half-deleted controls); orphan markers aren't written. `w:sdtPr` in schema order. A TOC's `docPartObj` stays owned by the TOC (rebuilt by the writer as before).
- **Editing**: deletions keep a marker whose partner lies outside the range (crossing a control's edge empties it rather than breaking it); copying half a control copies none of it. Typing into a control showing its placeholder replaces it; deleting all content brings the placeholder back (greyed `PlaceholderText` style). `sdtLocked` refuses deletion, `contentLocked` refuses edits (status message). Enter does nothing in one-line plain text / check box / drop-down. A caret at the edge of a control that takes no typing types beside it.

title: Layout and render: extreme page numbers and wave borders no longer overflow or run away
author: g1obalworlds
body:
Two small fixes for extreme numbers, found by a layout/PDF fuzzer (about 25 000 generated documents, built with overflow checks on).

**1. u32 overflow in page and line numbers** (`crates/layout/src/lib.rs`)
- `new_page` did `self.number += 1`. The page-number start comes from `w:pgNumType w:start`, which the .docx reader accepts up to 4294967295, so a document starting at 4294967295 with two or more pages panics with `attempt to add with overflow` in any build with overflow checks on (dev, test, some distro builds). In a plain release build the number silently wraps to 0.
- The line-number code did `pb.line_no += 1` and `pb.line_no + ln.start...`. The .docx path caps the start at 32767, but a value set through .json or commands is not capped.
- All three additions now use `saturating_add`.

**2. Endless wave stroke** (`crates/render/src/lib.rs`)
- The wave stroke (wave page borders and underlines) loops `while x < b && x - a < 20_000.0`. Once `|a|` passes about 1e16, `x + step == x`, so it never advances, and pushes curves until memory runs out ("memory allocation of 7516192768 bytes failed"). Reproduced with a wave page border whose `space` is 1e20 in a .json document; reachable through .json, the control channel and MCP (the .docx reader clamps `w:space` to 31 pt).
- The path is now built in a small `wave_path` function that stops as soon as a step makes no progress.

**Tests**
- `extreme_page_and_line_number_starts_do_not_overflow` (layout) lays out a three-page document with both starts at `u32::MAX`; without the fix it panics at `lib.rs` (`attempt to add with overflow`).
- `wave_stroke_at_a_huge_coordinate_ends` (render) checks `wave_path` for a 1e20 start, a 1e20-long wave and an ordinary one; without the guard the test aborts with the 7.5 GB allocation failure.

**Checked:** `cargo fmt`, `cargo test --workspace` (no failures), `cargo xtask assets`, `layers`, `wasm` and `parity` pass. I only had a 1.95 toolchain, not the pinned 1.90, so clippy on the whole wo…

title: Tables: Delete Columns never leaves a table with no rows
author: g1obalworlds
body:
Found by a stateful command fuzzer (about 30 million command runs, with the document checked for validity after every step).

**The bug.** `table.deleteCells` removes a cell without shrinking the grid or widening a neighbour, so a row can become shorter than `table.grid`. `table.deleteColumn` then deletes the grid column, which removes that row's only cell; `Table::delete_col` drops every row left without cells, so every row goes, and the command keeps the now empty table block (`rows: []`):

    wordcraft-cli run --template blank --cmd 'insert.table={"rows":1,"cols":2}' --cmd 'table.deleteCells={}' --cmd 'table.deleteColumn={}' --cmd 'document.inspect={}' --print

shows `{"type":"table","rows":0,"cols":1}`. Undo restores correctly and the .docx writer silently drops the empty table, so nothing crashes today, but anything that indexes `rows[0]` on that block would panic.

**The fix.** `del_col` removes the table when no rows are left, as it already does when the grid has a single column.

**Test.** `deleting_the_last_cell_column_never_leaves_a_table_without_rows` runs the sequence above, asserts no table block has zero rows (the emptied table is removed) and that undo brings it back. Without the fix it fails with `table without rows`.

**Checked:** `cargo fmt`, `cargo test --workspace` (no failures), `cargo xtask assets`, `layers`, `wasm` and `parity` pass. I only had a 1.95 toolchain, not the pinned 1.90, so clippy on the whole workspace stops at two lints that 1.95 added in code this PR doesn't touch (`collapsible_match`, `nonminimal_bool`); with those allowed it is clean. Please let CI confirm `cargo xtask ci` on 1.90. No open PR touches `del_col`.

title: Track Changes: formatting revisions (w:rPrChange/w:pPrChange) (#41)
author: vangel76
body:
## What

Formatting changes become tracked revisions, like insertions and deletions.

- **Model** (`crates/doc`): `PropChange<T>` (revision + properties before the change) on runs and paragraph marks (`CharProps::fmt_change`), paragraphs (`ParaProps::fmt_change`, plus `num_change` for `w:numberingChange`), tables, rows, cells and sections.
- **DOCX** (ECMA-376 §17.13.5): `w:rPrChange` (runs and paragraph-mark `w:rPr`), `w:pPrChange`, `w:numberingChange`, `w:tblPrChange`, `w:trPrChange`, `w:tcPrChange`, `w:sectPrChange` are read and written back, each as the last child of its parent. A change nested inside a change is ignored; `w:id`s are renumbered as for `w:ins`/`w:del`. Fixes the data loss reported in the issue (plain open + save dropped every `w:rPrChange`).
- **Recording**: with Track Changes and Track Formatting on, `Session::run` compares the paragraphs a command changed against the document before the command (paragraphs with the same text, Arc-shared ones skipped). So every formatting command (bold/italic/font/size/colour/highlight/styles/alignment/indents/spacing/lists/clear formatting…) records without per-command code. Same as Word: an author's later changes keep the formatting from before their first change, formatting set back to the original stops being a change, and formatting your own tracked insertion just changes the insertion. Accept/reject, compare, undo/redo and `file.*` don't record. Typed and pasted text doesn't carry a format change.
- **Accept/Reject**: at the caret (run, paragraph mark, paragraph, table cell), on a selection, and Accept All/Reject All. Accept keeps the new formatting and drops the record; reject puts back the old properties (links and ins/del marks stay, and so do cell merges and section headers/footers).
- **Review list**: Next/Previous Change and `review.changes` include format changes (`kind: "format"`, `description: "Formatted: Bold, Size: 14"` in our own wording, and `props` = the properties set). Neighbouring runs cha…

title: Document grid: lines per page and characters per line (#391)
author: vangel76
body:
## What

Layout › Page Setup › Document Grid (`w:docGrid`, ECMA-376 §17.6.5).

- **Model + DOCX**: `SectionProps::doc_grid` (type `default|lines|linesAndChars|snapToChars`, line pitch, `w:charSpace`) and paragraph `w:snapToGrid`, read and written (`w:docGrid` written after `w:bidi` in `sectPr`; Word's no-grid `<w:docGrid w:linePitch="360"/>` survives a round trip).
- **Layout**:
  - Line grid: in paragraphs that snap (the default; `w:snapToGrid w:val="0"` turns it off), each line's height rounds up to whole line pitches with the text centred in them. Multiple spacing is a multiple of the snapped height; Exactly isn't snapped. Headers and footers don't snap.
  - Character grid: `linesAndChars` gives East Asian characters (CJK ideographs, kana, Hangul, CJK punctuation, full-width forms) whole cells of the character pitch, glyph centred. The pitch is the Normal font size plus charSpace/4096 pt. A larger character takes `round(size / default size)` cells. Latin text keeps its own widths. With `snapToChars`, all text snaps to whole cells.
  - Hostile values (pitch 0, negative, NaN, huge; extreme charSpace) are clamped to 1–1584 pt.
  - The grid is part of the paragraph-layout cache key.
- **Command** `layout.documentGrid {"type"?, "linesPerPage"?, "charsPerLine"?, "linePitch"?, "charSpace"?}`: section scope like the other page-setup commands, one undo step, returns lines per page and characters per line. New catalog row: Layout › Page Setup › Document Grid (403/435).
- **UI**: the Page Setup dialog has a Document Grid section (no grid / lines only / lines and characters / text snaps to characters, characters per line, lines per page). When the section has a grid, View › Gridlines draws it instead of the drawing grid. New strings are in all 9 catalogs (including et, sr and sr-latn).

title: Track Changes: moves (w:moveFrom/w:moveTo) (#400)
author: vangel76
body:
Builds on #399 (now merged; rebased onto main).

Fixes #400

## What
Moved text is tracked as a move, not as a deletion plus an insertion (rest of gap #5's revision part).

- **Model:** `Revision::move_name` links a move's source (a deletion revision, `w:moveFrom`) and destination (an insertion revision, `w:moveTo`). Runs and paragraph marks keep their `ins`/`del` fields, so layout, PDF and the other formats keep treating moved-away text like a deletion (export shows the result).
- **DOCX** (ECMA-376 §17.13.5.21–28): `w:moveFrom`/`w:moveTo` inside `w:moveFromRangeStart/End` / `w:moveToRangeStart/End` are read as linked moves, moved paragraph marks included (their range starts in the paragraph content, so the mark is resolved after it). On save, the ranges are written around each moved stretch with name, author and date (ids renumbered, start/end ids matching), and moved-away text stays in `w:t`. Hostile input degrades: a move missing either end, a range that never ends, or a `w:moveFrom`/`w:moveTo` outside any range opens as a plain deletion/insertion. Open ranges and names are capped.
- **Recording:** with Track Changes on, `edit.cut` of a whole paragraph or at least a sentence gets a deletion revision of its own and is remembered; the `edit.paste` (or Paste Special › Formatted) right after it, by the same author with the same text, turns both into a move. Any other edit in between, undo or redo forgets it. A tracked paste now also marks the paragraph marks it adds as inserted.
- **Accept / Reject** at either end (caret or selection) resolves both ends: accept removes the source, reject removes the destination and restores the original position.
- **Reviewing Pane** (`review.changes`): kinds `moveFrom` / `moveTo`, with `move` (the name) and "Moved from" / "Moved to" descriptions.
